import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Formula α) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

instance : DeMorgan (Formula α) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  and := by simp
  or := by simp
  imply := by simp[imp_eq]
  neg := by simp

def complexity : Formula α → ℕ
| ⊤       => 0
| ⊥       => 0
| atom _  => 0
| natom _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Formula α) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_bot : complexity (⊥ : Formula α) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_atom (a : α) : complexity (atom a) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_natom (a : α) : complexity (natom a) = 0 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : complexity (φ ⋏ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_and' (φ ψ : Formula α) : complexity (and φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[simp] lemma complexity_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : complexity (φ ⋎ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl
@[simp] lemma complexity_or' (φ ψ : Formula α) : complexity (or φ ψ) = max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1 := rfl

@[elab_as_elim]
def cases' {C : Formula α → Sort w}
    (hverum  : C ⊤)
    (hfalsum : C ⊥)
    (hatom   : ∀ a : α, C (atom a))
    (hnatom  : ∀ a : α, C (natom a))
    (hand    : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C (φ ⋏ ψ))
    (hor     : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C (φ ⋎ ψ)) : (φ : Formula α) → C φ
  | ⊤       => hverum
  | ⊥       => hfalsum
  | atom a  => hatom a
  | natom a => hnatom a
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => hand φ ψ
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => hor φ ψ

@[elab_as_elim]
def rec' {C : Formula α → Sort w}
  (hverum  : C ⊤)
  (hfalsum : C ⊥)
  (hatom   : ∀ a : α, C (atom a))
  (hnatom  : ∀ a : α, C (natom a))
  (hand    : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C φ → C ψ → C (φ ⋏ ψ))
  (hor     : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C φ → C ψ → C (φ ⋎ ψ)) : (φ : Formula α) → C φ
  | ⊤       => hverum
  | ⊥       => hfalsum
  | atom a  => hatom a
  | natom a => hnatom a
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => hand φ ψ (rec' hverum hfalsum hatom hnatom hand hor φ) (rec' hverum hfalsum hatom hnatom hand hor ψ)
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => hor φ ψ (rec' hverum hfalsum hatom hnatom hand hor φ) (rec' hverum hfalsum hatom hnatom hand hor ψ)

@[simp] lemma complexity_neg (φ : Formula α) : complexity (∼φ) = complexity φ :=
  by induction φ using rec' <;> simp[*]

section Decidable

variable [DecidableEq α]

def hasDecEq : (φ ψ : Formula α) → Decidable (φ = ψ)
  | ⊤,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | ⊥,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | atom a,  ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | natom a, ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | φ ⋏ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hand φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])
  | φ ⋎ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hor φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])

instance : DecidableEq (Formula α) := hasDecEq

end Decidable

lemma ne_of_ne_complexity {φ ψ : Formula α} (h : φ.complexity ≠ ψ.complexity) : φ ≠ ψ :=
  by rintro rfl; contradiction

end Formula

abbrev Theory (α : Type*) := Set (Formula α)

instance : Collection (Formula α) (Theory α) := by exact?

/--
`inferInstance` synthesizes a value of any target type by typeclass
inference. This function has the same type signature as the identity
function, but the square brackets on the `[i : α]` argument means that it will
attempt to construct this argument by typeclass inference. (This will fail if
`α` is not a `class`.) Example:
```
#check (inferInstance : Inhabited Nat) -- Inhabited Nat

def foo : Inhabited (Nat × Nat) :=
  inferInstance

example : foo.default = (default, default) :=
  rfl
```
-/

namespace LO

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)

  | ⊤,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | ⊥,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | atom a,  ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | natom a, ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | φ ⋏ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hand φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>

          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)

      case hor φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"

  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  | ⊤,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | ⊥,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | atom a,  ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | natom a, ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | φ ⋏ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hand φ' ψ' =>

          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)

      case hor φ' ψ' =>

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

  imply := by simp[imp_eq]

def hasDecEq : (φ ψ : Formula α) → Decidable (φ = ψ)
  | ⊤,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | ⊥,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | atom a,  ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | natom a, ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | φ ⋏ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hand φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])
  | φ ⋎ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hor φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

def rec' {C : Formula α → Sort w}
  (hverum  : C ⊤)
  (hfalsum : C ⊥)
  (hatom   : ∀ a : α, C (atom a))
  (hnatom  : ∀ a : α, C (natom a))
  (hand    : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C φ → C ψ → C (φ ⋏ ψ))
  (hor     : ∀ (φ ψ : Formula α), C φ → C ψ → C (φ ⋎ ψ)) : (φ : Formula α) → C φ

  | ⊥       => hfalsum

variable [DecidableEq α]

def hasDecEq : (φ ψ : Formula α) → Decidable (φ = ψ)
  | ⊤,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | ⊥,       ψ => by cases ψ using cases' <;>
      { simp; try { exact isFalse not_false }; try { exact isTrue trivial } }
  | atom a,  ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | natom a, ψ => by
      cases ψ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      simp; exact decEq _ _
  | φ ⋏ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hand φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])
  | φ ⋎ ψ,   χ => by
      cases χ using cases' <;> try { simp; exact isFalse not_false }
      case hor φ' ψ' =>
        exact match hasDecEq φ φ' with
        | isTrue hp =>
          match hasDecEq ψ ψ' with
          | isTrue hq  => isTrue (hp ▸ hq ▸ rfl)
          | isFalse hq => isFalse (by simp[hp, hq])
        | isFalse hp => isFalse (by simp[hp])

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

instance : DeMorgan (Formula α) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  and := by simp
  or := by simp
  imply := by simp[imp_eq]
  neg := by simp

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Formula α) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

instance : DeMorgan (Formula α) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  and := by simp
  or := by simp
  imply := by simp[imp_eq]
  neg := by simp

def complexity : Formula α → ℕ
| ⊤       => 0

| atom _  => 0
| natom _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Formula α) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"

  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

  falsum := rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Formula α) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

instance : DeMorgan (Formula α) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  and := by simp
  or := by simp
  imply := by simp[imp_eq]
  neg := by simp

def complexity : Formula α → ℕ
| ⊤       => 0
| ⊥       => 0
| atom _  => 0
| natom _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

@[simp] lemma complexity_top : complexity (⊤ : Formula α) = 0 := rfl

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

@[simp] lemma neg_top : ∼(⊤ : Formula α) = ⊥ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_bot : ∼(⊥ : Formula α) = ⊤ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_atom (a : α) : ∼(atom a) = natom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_natom (a : α) : ∼(natom a) = atom a := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_and (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋏ ψ) = ∼φ ⋎ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_or (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼(φ ⋎ ψ) = ∼φ ⋏ ∼ψ := rfl

@[simp] lemma neg_neg' (φ : Formula α) : ∼∼φ = φ := neg_neg φ

@[simp] lemma neg_inj (φ ψ : Formula α) : ∼φ = ∼ψ ↔ φ = ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h; simpa using congr_arg (∼·) h
  · exact congr_arg _

lemma neg_eq (φ : Formula α) : ∼φ = neg φ := rfl

lemma imp_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ➝ ψ = ∼φ ⋎ ψ := rfl

lemma iff_eq (φ ψ : Formula α) : φ ⭤ ψ = (∼φ ⋎ ψ) ⋏ (∼ψ ⋎ φ) := rfl

@[simp] lemma and_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋏ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋏ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Wedge.wedge]

@[simp] lemma or_inj (φ₁ ψ₁ φ₂ ψ₂ : Formula α) : φ₁ ⋎ φ₂ = ψ₁ ⋎ ψ₂ ↔ φ₁ = ψ₁ ∧ φ₂ = ψ₂ :=
by simp[Vee.vee]

instance : DeMorgan (Formula α) where
  verum := rfl
  falsum := rfl
  and := by simp
  or := by simp
  imply := by simp[imp_eq]
  neg := by simp

def complexity : Formula α → ℕ
| ⊤       => 0
| ⊥       => 0
| atom _  => 0
| natom _ => 0
| φ ⋏ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1
| φ ⋎ ψ   => max φ.complexity ψ.complexity + 1

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

  wedge := and

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

namespace Propositional.Classical

  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

def toStr : Formula α → String
  | ⊤       => "\\top"
  | ⊥       => "\\bot"
  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | natom a => "\\lnot {" ++ toString a ++ "}"
  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

instance : LogicalConnective (Formula α) where
  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ
  wedge := and
  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum

section ToString

variable [ToString α]

  | atom a  => "{" ++ toString a ++ "}"

  | φ ⋏ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\land " ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"
  | φ ⋎ ψ   => "\\left(" ++ toStr φ ++ " \\lor "  ++ toStr ψ ++ "\\right)"

instance : Repr (Formula α) := ⟨fun t _ => toStr t⟩

instance : ToString (Formula α) := ⟨toStr⟩

end ToString

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

namespace LO

namespace Propositional.Classical

inductive Formula (α : Type u) : Type u where
  | verum  : Formula α
  | falsum : Formula α
  | atom   : α → Formula α
  | natom  : α → Formula α
  | and    : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α
  | or     : Formula α → Formula α → Formula α

namespace Formula

variable
  {α : Type u} {α₁ : Type u₁} {α₂ : Type u₂} {α₃ : Type u₃}

def neg : Formula α → Formula α
  | verum   => falsum
  | falsum  => verum
  | atom a  => natom a
  | natom a => atom a
  | and φ ψ => or (neg φ) (neg ψ)
  | or φ ψ  => and (neg φ) (neg ψ)

lemma neg_neg (φ : Formula α) : neg (neg φ) = φ :=
  by induction φ <;> simp[*, neg]

  tilde := neg
  arrow := fun φ ψ => or (neg φ) ψ

  vee := or
  top := verum
  bot := falsum
